programme: Two threads run through the concordant factors, and only these four factors carry them. First, JUN (AP-1) and MYC act as the RAS-MAPK/ERK proliferative output of FGFR2 signaling in cranial suture mesenchyme, driving the osteoprogenitor over-proliferation that closes sutures early. Second, HAND2 (acting downstream of Twist1 in the Twist1-Dlx5-Hand2 craniofacial patterning circuit) and HOXA13 (HOXA cluster) mark a genomic region around 7p21.1-p15 that, when deleted or duplicated as a block together with flanking genes, produces syndromic craniosynostosis-spectrum features plus developmental delay/intellectual disability in the same patients.
role_in_a: In craniosynostosis, JUN/AP-1 and MYC are the downstream proliferative/pro-survival effectors of FGFR2 gain-of-function signaling in suture mesenchyme (PMID 12815619, 19403560); HAND2 sits in the Twist1-Dlx5-Hand2 craniofacial patterning pathway whose disruption affects mandibular/cranial neural crest development (PMID 28769044, 22411303, 39707586); HOXA13 and its cluster are flagged when large deletions spanning the TWIST1 locus produce syndromic craniosynostosis (PMID 22570644, 29177010).
role_in_b: In intellectual disability, the same factors appear mostly as passengers of large chromosomal rearrangements rather than through a dedicated neurodevelopmental pathway: HOXA13 and HAND2 are named in patients whose 7p15/7p21.1-p14.3 or 1q43q44/4q32 deletions-duplications cause developmental delay alongside craniofacial anomalies (PMID 22570644, 29177010, 30410579, 24459084). MYC has a more direct route via the FMRP-STAT3-MYC axis controlling adult hippocampal neurogenesis, relevant to Fragile-X-associated intellectual disability (PMID 41385812, 40683950). JUN's ID evidence is thin — one case report implicates JNK signaling (JUN's upstream kinase) in a dysmorphic syndrome (PMID 39846792), not a direct JUN-ID link.
shared_axis: The two diseases most plausibly meet through contiguous-gene deletion/duplication at loci carrying HAND2- and HOXA13-pathway genes next to TWIST1: losing or gaining this block produces both the craniofacial suture phenotype and neurodevelopmental delay in the same patient, while JUN/MYC represent the separate RAS-MAPK proliferative checkpoint that is hyperactive in suture mesenchyme in craniosynostosis and, independently, regulated by FMRP in neural progenitors in Fragile-X-type intellectual disability.
reasoning: The programme is nameable and two of its four carrying factors (HOXA13, HAND2) are directly placed in case reports describing patients with both craniosynostosis-spectrum features and intellectual disability from the same deletion/duplication, which is genuine joint evidence rather than reasoning alone. But the connection is built from a handful of syndromic case reports at only 2 independent cohort pairs, JUN and MYC's ID evidence is either indirect (JNK, not JUN itself) or drawn from a different mechanism (FMRP-MYC neurogenesis) than their craniosynostosis role, and six of the twelve listed factors (ELF5, NR5A2, NR5A1, LYL1, ZNF354C, ZNF202) have no evidence in either disease at all — so the recurrence signal outruns what the retrieved literature actually supports.
support: PMID 12815619 — AP-1/c-Jun downstream of FGF2-ERK drives premature cranial suture closure. PMID 19403560 — MYC implicated in FGFR2-mutant senescence/prosurvival signaling in craniosynostosis. PMID 22570644 — 7p21.1-p14.3 microdeletion spanning TWIST gene causes severe developmental delay (joint craniosynostosis-region/ID evidence). PMID 29177010 — 7p15 (HOXA-region) deletion reported with both craniosynostosis-spectrum and ID features (explicit joint evidence). PMID 28769044, 22411303, 39707586 — Twist1-Dlx5-Hand2 pathway papers placing HAND2 in craniofacial/mandibular neural crest development. PMID 30410579 — 1q43q44 deletion/4q32.1q35.2 duplication patient with combined craniofacial and ID phenotype (joint evidence for HAND2 region). PMID 24459084 — distal 4q duplication patients characterized for ID (HAND2 region). PMID 41385812, 40683950 — FMRP-STAT3-MYC axis in Fragile-X-related neurogenesis/ID. PMID 39846792 — JNK-signaling-linked dysmorphic syndrome, weak indirect JUN-ID evidence.
how_to_falsify: In craniosynostosis patients with isolated FGFR2 gain-of-function mutations and no 7p21.1-p15, 1q43q44, or 4q32 deletion/duplication, check whether intellectual disability rates and JUN/MYC target-gene activation in suture tissue are no different from deletion-negative controls. If ID is confined entirely to the deletion/duplication-positive subgroup and JUN/MYC activity shows no relationship to cognitive outcome in the deletion-negative group, the proposed proliferative (RAS-MAPK/MYC) contribution to ID is false and the whole comorbidity reduces to contiguous gene loss at HAND2/HOXA13-adjacent loci.
caveats: Only 15 patient-group comparisons drawn from 2 independent cohort pairs, and the tissue pairing (blood|bone) means the network was not estimated directly in cranial suture or brain tissue, so factor concordance is a blood/bone proxy rather than direct evidence in the disease-relevant cells. HAND2, HOXA13, JUN and MYC all lack a recorded Open Targets association with craniosynostosis (or the association is weak, e.g. HOXA13 at percentile 0.81), so curated disease-gene databases do not independently corroborate this account; the literature support instead comes from a small number of syndromic case reports. Six of the twelve concordant factors (ELF5, NR5A2, NR5A1, LYL1, ZNF354C, ZNF202) have no textual evidence in either disease despite 13-15/15 concordance, so this account explains only a third of the recurring factors. The single-view exclusions (STAT1, IKZF1, EBF1, MED23, BHLHE22) and tissue-generic exclusions (IKZF1, STAT1, IRF1, NFATC1, CIITA, NR4A3, etc. — largely immune/lymphoid regulators) confirm that an immune-cell master-regulator story was correctly screened out; this account should not be read as an immune mechanism.
